newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Enterprises urges power mkt equity.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Enterprises urges power mkt equity.

text.p: Pacific Enterprises (PE), the parent of Southern California Gas Co, urged federal lawmakers to take immediate legislative action on unresolved issues of power transmission and generation equity, the company said on Friday.

At a Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee workshop on Thursday, George Minter, PE's director of public policy, said "it's important to note that the delivered price of electricity will be the basis for customer choice."

As a result, Congress must address transmission pricing policy in federal restructuring legislation in order to guide the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), which cannot consider cost causation, equity or economic efficiency--issues that are critical to a competitive energy services market, Minter said.

The company also called for a reciprocity clause, meaning that markets which have provided for retail competition would only be open to out-of-state market participants from states that have also enacted retail choice.

Minter also pointed out the power exchange system being proposed for California, which is now being reviewed by FERC, calls for a utility-specific, single access fee paid by consumers to recover most transmission revenue requirements.
Pacific Enterprises believes such an approach unfairly penalizes local generation since all users end up carrying the costs of long-distance transmission.

Minter also told the committee that Congress must address a generation inequity which will allow older base-load coal generation plants to produce cheaper power than gas-fired generation, thus denying gas a level playing field.

Under federal Clean Air Act amendments, these older coal plants were not required to install the expensive emission control equipment that newer plants had to install, giving the coal units a price advantage when bidding into competitive power markets, the company contended.

Minter said Congress can address this inequity by requiring generators that bid into a competitive power market to meet current emissions standards for that increment of power that is bid into the market.
